transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because the last few weeks, I’ve had this heavy sadness on me almost all day. I’m still smiling and doing my job with patients, but inside it feels like I’m barely holding myself together.
You mentioned this has been going on for a few weeks—can you tell me the exact day or week it started?
It started about three weeks ago, shortly after I found out I was pregnant.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks of persistent low mood or loss of interest—prior to this pregnancy?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember having a stretch like this before.
Over these past three weeks, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy, even when you're not at work?
Yeah. After my shifts, I used to paint or go to yoga or salsa to decompress. Lately I just go home and sit on the couch. I ignore texts too—it all just feels like more effort than it’s worth.
Over the past three weeks, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up much earlier than usual?
I’m not sure—I haven’t really paid close attention to my sleep lately.
In the past three weeks, have you had any thoughts of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or thoughts of harming yourself?
I’ve had thoughts like… wishing I just wouldn’t wake up. That’s what scared me enough to say something at my prenatal appointment. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, though.
Even though you're still going to work, have you noticed it's become harder to concentrate, keep up with your usual pace, or complete your tasks as a nurse compared to before?
Yeah. I keep rereading medication orders and wound-care notes because my brain feels foggy. Things I’d normally decide automatically, I just freeze and second-guess myself.
Would you say these symptoms have made it just harder to get through your daily activities, or have they actually stopped you from managing your usual responsibilities at home and work?

I’m still making it to work, but it’s not just harder. My supervisor has noticed my charting isn’t getting finished, and I’ve been pulling away from my friends and the things that usually help keep me steady.
Over the past three weeks, how often have you had those thoughts of wishing you wouldn't wake up—would you say it's just occasional, or does it happen nearly every day?
It’s been happening nearly every day. Just that thought of not wanting to wake up—not that I have a plan to do anything.

Beyond work, how are you managing basic day-to-day things like cooking, cleaning, or taking care of yourself—are you still able to keep up with most of that, or has it become hard to manage almost everything right now?

I’m still getting to work, but I’m not keeping up like I normally do. My supervisor’s already noticed I’m leaving charting incomplete, and outside of work I’ve been pulling away from my friends and the things that usually keep me grounded.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a 3-week history of persistent depressed mood, marked anhedonia (withdrawal from painting, yoga, salsa, socializing), cognitive impairment (poor concentration, indecisiveness affecting nursing duties), and near-daily passive suicidal ideation ('wishing I wouldn't wake up') without a specific plan. Functional impairment is evident through incomplete charting noted by her supervisor and social withdrawal, though she remains able to attend work. Onset occurred shortly after learning of pregnancy, a significant psychosocial stressor, but the depressive syndrome meets full criteria independent of a formal peripartum-onset specifier discussion in this transcript. The combination of ≥5 symptoms including suicidal ideation, cognitive symptoms, and clear functional impairment (though not complete incapacitation) with no psychotic features supports a severe single depressive episode without psychotic symptoms (F32.2) rather than moderate (F32.1). No mania/hypomania history reported, ruling out bipolar spectrum; no primary sleep-only complaint to support insomnia disorder alone.
